name: Conditioning-Minimal Non-Ample Classes Are Not Projection-Closed
statement: Let $H$ have $n$ active coordinates and VC dimension $k$. Its projection to $Z$ is $Q_Z$ when $|Z|\le k$, is $Q_Z$ with one antipodal pair removed when $|Z|=k+1$, and is again conditioning-minimal non-ample of VC dimension $k$ when $|Z|>k+1$. Hence the class is not projection-closed.
proof: The uniform-oriented-matroid classification identifies projection with deletion. Deleting to at most the rank gives the free matroid and a cube; deletion to rank plus one leaves exactly one antipodal pair absent; larger deletions remain non-free uniform oriented matroids and hence conditioning-minimal non-ample.
